sentences.text: Brief facts of the case are that on 08.10.1993, police Juni Indore received information from MY Hospital that Madhu W/o Harish has been admitted in hospital in burn condition.

Then,
information was registered at Roznamcha No.65.
On 09.10.1993, police investigated the matter.
During treatment, Madhu was declared dead on 14.10.1993.
Police investigated the matter and after due investigation, filed charge-sheet before the competent court under Section 304B of IPC.
3. Trial court framed charges against the appellant which were denied by the appellant.
Trial court found the appellant guilty under Section 498A of IPC and convicted him as aforesaid.
Appellant filed this appeal being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and submitted that trial court has committed error in law and facts in convicting him under Section 498A of IPC.
There is no reliable evidence on record.
There are so many contradictions and omissions in the statements of prosecution witnesses so their evidence could not be reliable.
So on these grounds, appellant prays for setting aside the judgment and prays for his acquittal.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent/State supported the impugned judgment and prays for rejection of the appeal.
5. Now, question arises whether trial court has committed error in convicting the appellant under Section 498A of IPC.

6. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.
7.
It is undisputed that deceased- Madhu was wife of the appellant --3-- and her death occurred within 7 years of her marriage.

Considering the evidence of PW-1 Gopaldas,
PW-9 Lajvanti, PW-12 Basudev and PW-13 Prakash, it is found that they have categorically stated in their evidence that appellant demanded dowry and tortured his wife for demand of dowry.

They were cross-examined at length and on perusal of their cross- examination, it is found that they are intact in their cross-examination and there is no substantial contradiction and omission found in their cross- examination and there is no reason to disbelieve their evidence.
So considering the evidence of the prosecution witnesses, this Court finds that they are reliable and cogent.
They are intact in their cross- examination and they are corroborated each other.
So, considering the evidence of prosecution witnesses, in the considered opinion of this court, trial court has not committed any error in convicting the appellant under Section 498A of IPC.
8. Appellant was 26 years old at the time of the incident and now he is about 60 years old.
Record of the trial court does not show that he was earlier convicted in any case so it seems that appellant is first offender.
He is an earning member of his family.
He has been regularly appearing before the concerned court on the dates so fixed.

At this juncture, after 33 years, if the appellant is sent to jail,

Appellant was under judicial custody from 09.12.1993 to 24.12.1993.
He has deposited fine amount of Rs.1000/- before the trial court.
So far as his sentence is concerned, looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, the appellant has already undergone some period in jail and he is facing case from 1993

, hence, to meet the interest of justice,
appellant is sentenced to the period already undergone --4-- by him along with the fine imposed by the trial court.
His bail bonds stand cancelled.
This appeal is partly allowed.
